name: pickle lentil relish
instructions:
PICKLE LENTIL RELISH — the ale + pickle lentil stew, split out 2026-11-20 from [[pub-style-lentils]] (where it was Build 2, the pureed-mushroom gravy stew). Built on the PUREED-MUSHROOM GRAVY CORE (pureed mushrooms + whole lentils + tomato paste + dark bouillon + butter + flour), with DARK ALE + PICKLE JUICE + CUMIN/CARAWAY SEEDS doing the flavor injection.

1. SAUTÉ onions + garlic in BUTTER with the CUMIN and/or CARAWAY SEEDS blooming in the fat. (Add diced turnips here if using.)
2. PUREED MUSHROOMS (cremini or portabella): add the mushroom paste (food processor or blender) and cook it down.
3. FLOUR over the base, stir to coat (light roux).
4. DEGLAZE WITH DARK ALE (milk stout preferred — see the anchor note). Let it reduce briefly.
5. TOMATO PASTE + DARK BROTH + WORCESTERSHIRE: the vegetarian beef-stew backbone.
6. LENTILS in; simmer until tender (turnips soften alongside).
7. TANG: PICKLE JUICE to taste, then DICED DILL PICKLES.
8. FINISH WITH SWEET PEAS, folded in at the end.
9. Serve as a stew; or top with mash + melting CHEDDAR and bake for the cottage-pie format.
notes:
=== SPLIT OUT (2026-11-20) ===

Split from [[pub-style-lentils]], where it lived as the ale + pickle build since the 2026-11-02 merge (its pre-merge original was mushroom pickle relish). The jamie file keeps the marmite line; this file is the ale + pickle line.

=== PAIRING — PORK AND HOT-DOG-LIKE THINGS ===

A good relish for PORK and HOT-DOG-LIKE THINGS — rather than potatoes, which are the natural pairing for the pub lentil relish ([[pub-style-lentils]], served on baked potatoes).

=== THE ANCHOR — DARK ALE, MILK STOUT PREFERRED ===

Dark ale is the bitter anchor. MILK STOUT preferred — regular stout's bitterness compounds; milk stout's lactose sweetness keeps the bitterness budget in balance (the Nigella milk-stout-oxtail lesson, shared with [[milk-stout-braised-beef]]). The dark bouillon in the gravy core rides UNDER the ale — it is not a second anchor; one anchor only.

=== THE ANGLO-GERMANIC INJECTION — ALE + PICKLE + SEED-SPICE ===

- PICKLE JUICE + DICED DILL PICKLES: the register's tang — the german sour-into-the-braise logic (Linsensuppe's canonical vinegar finish, sauerbraten thinking); pickle juice is vinegar with the dill axis pre-bundled. The tang is pickle, not cream (cream clashing). DIJON moved to secondary 2026-11-20 (mustard + ale was always the untested carbonnade edge).
- CUMIN AND/OR CARAWAY SEEDS bloomed in the butter. Cumin is the tested default; CARAWAY is the german cousin (carvone — the same aroma family as dill seed, so it harmonizes with the pickle axis). SEEDS ONLY, never ground powder on top. Caraway works here even though it's clashing in [[pub-style-lentils]] (the leftovers test there).

=== CARROTS (2026-11-20) ===

Carrots are want-to-try here tbh — I think there's a pairing there. (They stay out of the jamie version, which doesn't want them.)

=== TOMATO — NECESSARY BUT SHOULDN'T BE TASTED ===

The finished stew reads DARK, not red. This build takes MORE tomato paste than the french sibling (the bitter base fights tomato, so it takes more to hold the warmth leg) even though it looks darker. Calibrate by register, not color.

=== IF OVER-SPICED ===

Lemon juice/zest is the rescue — it pulls it back old-world; NOT ginger, wrong register.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[pub-style-lentils]]: the Jamie Oliver marmite line this split from — the lemon + cumin + rosemary engine, served on baked potatoes.
- [[french-lentils]]: the same gravy core with the french injection (mustard + cream + potato). The contrast pair.
- [[milk-stout-braised-beef]]: the meat expression of this register (oxtail/short rib + milk stout + a dill pickle in the braise).
- [[relish]]: the standalone condiment expression of the pickle-tang axis.
- [[shittake-lentil-soup]]: the clean dark-stock soup cousin.
original_chef: Mine — descends from Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie line, converged toward german Linsensuppe logic.
